column1: # scope-map.tsv — which requirements V1 deliberately does not implement
# Without it the report says "177 of 245 requirements have no automated test"
# and lists them flat. That is true and misleading: it puts BE-01 (a route on a
# server V1 never builds) next to LD-02 (lap detection, shipped, running on
# phones today, genuinely untested). A reader cannot tell a scope decision from
# neglect, so they assume the worst about everything — including the parts that
# This file separates the two. It does not excuse anything: requirements listed
# here stay in the document, keep their own count, and are printed in full.
#   scope   V2-BACKEND  Cannot be built or tested in V1: it needs a server,
#                       Firebase, or a hosted model, none of which V1 has.
#           V1          An explicit override. Beats a section line above it.
#   target  @Section    Every requirement in that SRS section (exact heading
#           XX-01       One requirement. Always wins over a section line.
#   reason  Free text, shown verbatim in the report. Say why, not what.
# Look at the subject of the sentence.
#   "The backend shall ..."  -> V2-BACKEND. Nothing to run it on.
#   "The app shall ..."      -> V1, even when the sentence mentions upload.
# The client half of a network feature is testable against a fake server, and
# some of it already is: TU-04, TU-06 and TU-07 pass today against MockWebServer.
# Marking them deferred would be hiding work that is done.
# The report refuses to let this file be used as a rug:
#   * A requirement marked V2-BACKEND that has a PASSING test is an error.
#     Either this note is stale, or we built something we said we had not.
#   * A target that names no section or requirement in the SRS is an error.
#   * V2-BACKEND requirements are never removed from the document. Both
#     denominators — all requirements, and V1 requirements — are always printed
# Out-of-scope items (OOS-*) are not listed here. "We will never build this" is
# already handled by excluding that SRS section entirely; this file is only for
# SRS §2 states the whole section is deferred; V1 runs single-user and offline
# with a local driver profile (§2a) instead.
